correctness.rationale: Conditional independence of receivers gives exact two-state ODE. Independent source lifetime sums give Eq.(2) variance O(1/log n), exact mean Eq.(3). The depletion correction has vanishing expectation at scale n via explicit two-source covariance Eq.(4). Thus conditional infected receivers converge to Poisson with parameter lambda Phi(theta) exp(-x), and all sources survive with probability O(1/log n). Absorbing-state identity yields Gumbel. 144 independent finite-generator matrix exponential checks and 3 large-system simulations passed; experiments not proof.

value.rationale: The physical fading time of a two-stage directed epidemic displays a nontrivial loglog delay, Gumbel limiting shape, and explicit crossover on shrinking rate-difference scale 1/log n. It identifies a natural resonance boundary not visible in standard single-decay exponential tail estimates. The full distribution, not only mean extinction, is determined; the model assumptions are motivated by feedforward infection and identifiable graph topology.
